newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada expects Haiti force extension to mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: Canada expects Haiti force extension to mid-1997.

text.p: Canada expects the U.N. peacekeeping mission in Haiti will be extended for another seven months, Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Tuesday.
Axworthy told a parliamentary committee that he expected China, which has hampered previous U.N. Security Council resolutions regarding Haiti, would likely agree to the extension.
"It is not possible to provide you with a 100 percent guarantee. However, my perception is that the Chinese are willing to continue the mission in Haiti," Axworthy said.
The United Nations took over the Haiti operation in March 1995 from 20,000 U.S. troops who restored former president Jean-Bertrand Aristide to power in October 1994.
About 1,600 U.N. peacekeepers are currently in Haiti. Their mandate, renewed at the end of June, expires at the end of November and the plan is to extend it to June 30, 1997.
Haitian President Rene Preval last week requested an extension to give the Haitian National Police more time to gain experience in maintaining order.
China, angry at Haiti's diplomatic ties to Taiwan which it considers a renegade province, has previously expressed reservations on the continued presence of U.N. personnel in Haiti.
